summary.intent: Debug and fix a stale file content issue where the FUSE-mounted desktop folder showed the original version of a file after it had been edited and saved via the web UI.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified and fixed in `crates/fuse/src/inode.rs` (populate_folder never re-resolved already-resolved files), web UI fixed to republish folder metadata after edits (was only happening during IPNS key migration), and a cross-client sync E2E test suite added to prevent regressions.

repo: FUSE inode resolution uses a TTL-based metadata refresh (30s) via drain_refresh_completions + populate_folder; resolved files were never re-fetched because file_meta_resolved: true skipped the re-resolution path
The web UI's useFileOperations.ts only republished folder metadata during IPNS key migration, not on normal file edits — meaning modified_at on FilePointers was never updated for other clients
The content cache is keyed by CID (content-addressed), so it correctly handles different CIDs — the bug was upstream: stale CID references, not cache pollution
The SDK's uploadFile creates a new file with a new IPNS keypair; editing an existing file requires updateFileMetadata to update the existing file's IPNS record instead
Root folder IPNS keypair is derived via deriveVaultIpnsKeypair(userKeypair.privateKey) rather than stored directly
The @cipherbox/api-client generated dist was stale (missing publicKey on PublishIpnsDto) and required running api:generate to fix a type error that appeared pre-existing

Desktop E2E tests live in tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/ and use shell scripts pointing the SDK at a local dev instance; round-trip tests already existed for FUSE upload→SDK read but not SDK edit→FUSE read

code.finding: populate_folder() preserved existing InodeKind wholesale for file_meta_resolved: true inodes, never comparing modified_at. Fix: compare incoming modified_at with existing mtime; if different (!= after clock-skew review), reset to file_meta_resolved: false and preserve ipns_private_key + file_meta_ipns_name for re-resolution

Initial fix used > for modified_at comparison; changed to != after reviewer flagged clock skew risk — a file restored to older content would have a smaller modified_at and should also trigger re-resolution

updateFolderMetadataAndPublish was only called during IPNS key migration path. Fixed to always call it after a file edit so modified_at on the FilePointer propagates to polling clients (FUSE, other web sessions)
Argument parsing for --new-content used truthiness check, which rejected empty string. Fixed to use explicit undefined check so emptying a file's content is a valid operation

workflow: The gsd-debugger subagent pattern isolates investigation context (200k fresh context per investigation) — effective for bugs requiring extensive file reading and hypothesis testing
Phantom Cargo.lock diffs (cipherbox-fuse version bumped without Cargo.toml changes) appeared twice and needed manual revert before committing
Stale generated client dists can produce misleading type errors that appear pre-existing; always regenerate before ruling out a type error
Pre-existing type errors on main should be verified with git stash + typecheck before assuming a new change caused them
1Password SSH agent signing failures can block git commits silently with an API error; staged files survive the failure

friction: git commit failed with a 1Password SSH agent signing error (Internal server error), leaving staged changes uncommitted and requiring a manual retry
Cargo.lock phantom diff appeared twice across two separate commits, requiring manual revert each time
Stale @cipherbox/api-client dist caused a misleading PublishIpnsDto type error that looked pre-existing but was actually a build artifact requiring api:generate to fix

The web UI folder metadata republish gap (the deeper root cause for cross-client sync) was only discovered while writing E2E tests, not during the initial FUSE fix — the FUSE fix alone would not have fully resolved the user's issue
open_items: E2E test (test-cross-client-sync.sh) requires a live desktop app with FUSE mount + running dev instance — not yet wired into CI; needs a CI strategy

The replaced-FilePointer case with same modified_at is not handled (intentionally — same modified_at implies no change) but could be a subtle edge case if a file is deleted and re-uploaded within the same second
The cross-client sync test waits 30-60s for IPNS poll cycle — this makes it slow for CI; consider whether the poll TTL should be configurable for test environments

Clock skew between client and server could still cause missed updates if clocks diverge enough that a newer file appears to have the same or older modified_at — no mitigation implemented beyond the != comparison
